what: Round 15 (review 4, M2; approved by the owner): Power of Siberia gas to China, actual and contracted, in bcm a year. The pipeline was agreed in 2014 (CNPC-Gazprom 30-year contract, 38 bcm/yr plateau) and has flowed since December 2019, so its contracted ramp-up was expected without the war: China's no-war imports from Russia include the contracted volumes above the 2021 level. Only deliveries beyond the contracted path count as war-driven.
unit: bcm per year (2026: the 38 bcm/yr annual rate; the map takes January-August)

basis.2021: Gazprom, 10.39 bcm (gas_prices.json records 10.4 from Gazprom's project page; the figure 10.39 is the one approved by the owner; not re-fetched in round 15)
basis.2022: actual 15.4 bcm (Gazprom via Reuters, 3 January 2024); the 2022 contractual quantity was not found, so the actual delivery is taken as contracted (not verified)
basis.2023: 22.0 = 22.7 / 1.032: Gazprom said 2023 deliveries were 0.7 bcm (3.2%) above its contractual obligation (Reuters via BusinessDay, 3 January 2024; fetched)
basis.2024: 30.0: the initial plan for 2024 as reported by Interfax (31.12 bcm delivered against a plan of 30 bcm; seen in a search summary, page not fetched: not verified)
basis.2025: 38.0: the contractual plateau, reached from 1 December 2024 (Interfax, 13 January 2026; fetched); 38.84 bcm delivered, 0.84 bcm above plan (Interfax, 28 April 2026; fetched)
basis.2026: 38.0: the plateau; the later agreement to raise it to 44 bcm/yr (autumn 2025) was made during the war and is not in the no-war path

price_prewar_eur_mwh: 2019-2021 average of China's pipeline-gas unit value (gas_prices.json CHN pipeline: 18.0, 16.1, 11.6 EUR/MWh = 15.23); 10.55 TWh per bcm (MWH_PER_BCM in build_data.py)

sources.name: Interfax: Gazprom supplies 38.8 bcm of gas to China in 2025 (31.12 bcm in 2024; maximum contractual level of 38 bcm/yr from 1 December 2024)
Interfax: Power of Siberia at the planned contractual level of 38 bcm; 38.8 bcm in 2025 exceeded the contractual obligations
Reuters via BusinessDay: Russian gas supply to China reaches record daily level (22.7 bcm in 2023, 15.4 in 2022; 0.7 bcm above the contractual obligation)
TASS: Gazprom to supply over 38 bcm of gas via Power of Siberia to China in 2025; agreement to raise supplies to 44 bcm/yr
